_what: Hand-authored ground truth: for each fixture specification, which claims from the property
catalog its text actually makes. Authored by reading all thirteen specifications, not by
running anything. This exists to measure LAYER 2 (model extraction), and nothing else — it is
not a grade, not a rubric for learners, and never shown as one.
Why it is needed: the extractor is reproducible (five runs at temperature 0 agreed verbatim)
and that says nothing about whether it is RIGHT. It answered NO to claim 2 on the strongest
spec in the corpus, which states that claim twice. Without a key, an error like that is
indistinguishable from a weak specification, and the tool blames the learner for its own miss.

_verdicts.yes: the text asserts the claim (as a rule, or pinned unambiguously by a worked example)
_verdicts.no: the text is silent — it neither asserts nor denies it
_verdicts.contra: the text asserts something INCOMPATIBLE with the claim

_why_three: Silence and contradiction are different facts about a specification and they have different
consequences downstream. A silent spec leaves an implementer free; a contradicting spec sends
them the wrong way and the property will fail against any conforming implementation. Two
values would have collapsed them, and four of the six written fixtures use the third.
_out_of_scope: Claims a fixture's own brief never put in front of its author. A basic-tier spec is silent
about BestOf and OnlyIf because the basic brief has no such rules — that is correct work, not
a gap. The extractor should still answer NO; the distinction matters only when the report is
read by a person. Same trap as the surface check, which used to read the codebase instead of
the brief and flagged basic specs for omitting combinators they were never shown.
_claims: an empty rule list leaves the price alone
no rule ever raises the price
a percentage subtracts a rounded-down discount
rules compound — each sees what the one before it left
the big-spender bonus reads the price it is applied to
a large price does not overflow
BestOf hands over the lowest of its options
OnlyIf leaves a duck its condition rejects untouched
